findings.claim: The q1 rationale quotes option A in single quotation marks in a form that does not exist verbatim on the sheet: it drops the word 'lifting'. A second, lesser instance in the same rationale silently lowercases the passage's sentence-initial word inside a double-quoted passage citation.
findings.evidence: Rationale q1: "A (over-hedge/mis-scope) tempts because the quote is hedged – but ‘could not settle where the force was coming from’ contradicts the mapped result". Option A reads: "Her cores could not settle where the lifting force was coming from." Programmatic verbatim sweep over passage + all five stems + all twenty options: the string 'could not settle where the force was coming from' returns exact=False, case-insensitive=False, i.e. it exists nowhere in the unit. The same sweep returns exact=False / ci=True for “most of the force, we think, is generated within a hand’s width of the stone”, because the passage reads “Most of the force…”. All sixteen other quoted strings across the five rationales (including the repaired q4 verdict sentence, 'The five had one thing in common', 'The surveys measure the stones, and only the stones', 'We are reading the flags, not the roots', 'For all we know, the bedding on the good streets is filling with root', 'on the whole, with a few exceptions', 'the remedies keep failing', 'how one city’s remedy has fared') verify exact=True.
findings.why: The rationale is student-facing teaching payload and the single quotation marks assert a citation. G-REGISTER-releg charged exactly this class of defect as a major in fleet-repair-1 on the ground that 'a learner told to find [the quoted words] will search the passage for words that were deleted'. Here the miss is one word inside an option sitting on the same sheet, so the learner recovers it instantly and no reasoning changes — hence minor, not major. It is nevertheless the one quote-fidelity residual that survived three repair rounds and two dedicated quote sweeps (fleet-repair-1's 'rationale sync', fleet-repair-3's 'full-unit residual probe'), both of which searched only for the q4 verdict sentence.

findings.claim: The fleet-repair-3 record overstates what its ¶4 reattribution achieved: it claims to have removed 'the one line a solver could have used to argue q3-C from the passage', but the line that actually funds q3-C was never touched, and the same round's own G-DISTRACTOR record cites it by name.
findings.evidence: gen-elf-long.NOTES.md, fleet-repair-3: "The round-3 edits move both floors in the solver's disfavour rather than in his favour: naming Fearnbeck removes a free referent inference on q4, and reattributing the root finding removes the one line a solver could have used to argue q3-C from the passage." The untouched ¶4 clause is "the thin, stiff beds elsewhere were apparently not worth the climb", and verdicts/verdicts-gdistractor-r3.jsonl (same round, 12:00:30Z) records for q:3: "Counsel's best case cites the paragraph-4 aside \"the thin, stiff beds elsewhere were apparently not worth the climb\" (which places the roots below the bedding on the twenty-five) … reattributing the paragraph-4 lift to \"the crews\" does not strengthen this option." Byte diff of the passage between gen-elf-long.json (round 0) and candidates/elf-b18-001.json confirms exactly two sentence-level changes, neither of which is that clause.
findings.why: The repair's actor fix (survey → crews) is real and is correctly verified by G-REGISTER-r3: nothing in ¶4 now credits the April surveys with sub-stone knowledge. But the epistemic tension that funds q3-C is not an actor problem. ¶4 asserts, in the narrator's voice and hedged with 'apparently', a state of the bedding on streets that were never opened; ¶5 then says 'For all we know, the bedding on the good streets is filling with root that has not yet found its strength'. That pair survives round 3 intact. Recording the repair as having closed a residual it did not close is the defect — a downstream reader trusting the NOTES would not know to look. No key moves (see note on ¶4/¶5 friction), so minor.

findings.claim: A major flag raised against q1-C in round 2 was dropped in round 3 with an empty findings list, on byte-identical option text, with no recorded disposition — so the unit's thinnest answer margin leaves no trace in the shipping record.
findings.evidence: verdicts/verdicts-gdistractor-r2.jsonl, q:1, verdict 'flag', severity 'major', quote "Her digs showed the soil further down to be bare of living root.", note: "ARGUABLE… Beatable, but the entire defence rests on the single word 'almost', which is thinner than anything else on these three sheets." verdicts/verdicts-gdistractor-r3.jsonl, q:1: {"verdict": "pass", "findings": []}. fleet-repair-3 touched the passage only (two sentences, verified by byte diff); q1-C is byte-identical across gen-elf-long.json's post-repair-2 state and the shipped candidate. report-final.json's 'flags' array for elf-b18-001 carries the five G-STEM majors and nothing from G-DISTRACTOR.
findings.why: A fresh blind run is entitled to re-adjudicate, but a major that disappears with findings:[] on unchanged bytes and no disposition line is indistinguishable from an oversight, and it removes the residual from every downstream artefact. This is the same pattern the batch17 audit charged as minor on las-b17-001 q4 ('the unit-level review record shows no trace of the G-STEM major flag, so a downstream reader cannot see that Q4's difficulty rests partly on form'). The margin itself is defensible — six independent blind solves all returned B and all named the same defeater — so this is a record-keeping charge, not a correctness one.

findings.claim: The shipped unit declares blind floors that the last independent blind stem read contradicts, and G-STEM was never re-run after that read, so five majors ship undisposed against a self-declaration that is more favourable than the evidence.
findings.evidence: gen-elf-long.NOTES.md (fleet-repair-2, restated verbatim in fleet-repair-3): "q3: no better than 1-in-4 on form… q2/q4: no better than 1-in-4 on form", with no floor stated for q1. verdicts/verdicts-gstem-r2.jsonl, executed on the post-fleet-repair-2 sheet (it quotes the repaired option strings), returns 'flag'/major on all five questions, including q:1 "Narrowing 4->2 passage-blind; the passage still decides B vs C" and q:3 "A and C are mutually undercutting … Narrowing 4->2 passage-blind." verdicts/verdicts-gstem-r3.jsonl contains no elf-b18-001 row at all (only las-b18-002 and las-b18-003). report-final.json: "status": "SURVIVED_FLAGGED" with those five G-STEM majors as the entire flags array.
findings.why: The self-declared floor is the instrument the batch16 stance-composition policy conditions on — note severity is granted only 'provided (a) the adversarial blind floor is stated explicitly and is no better than 1-in-2'. The measured floors (1-in-2 on q1 and q3) do satisfy that condition, so the unit stays inside policy and the flags are correctly weighed at note severity below. The charge is narrower: the shipped record states 1-in-4 where the gate measured 1-in-2, and no round-3 G-STEM re-run reconciles the two. Anyone reading generator_meta or the NOTES without opening verdicts-gstem-r2.jsonl would believe the form floor is twice as strong as it is.

findings.claim: The q5 rationale's charge against option A — that 'rising' is not stated — rests on one reading of an ambiguous ¶1 sentence; under the competing and quite natural reading the passage does state that the cost rises, which would make A a verbatim-true distractor and void the law-11 justification the NOTES give for it.
findings.evidence: Rationale q5: "A promotes the vivid paragraph-1 claims detail to main topic – and distorts it slightly (‘rising’ is not stated)." generator_meta.engineered_traps.q5 repeats it ("A detail-as-main with a small distortion (‘rising’)"), and gen-elf-long.NOTES.md makes it a compliance claim: "A = detail-as-main with a small distortion ('rising' cost is not stated — law 11 discipline: no verbatim-true distractor)". The ¶1 sentence is: "In the mid-sized city where what follows took place, compensation for trips over lifted paving costs more each year than the parks department spends on planting." Option A: "The rising cost to councils of people tripping over uneven paving."
findings.why: The generator's reading — 'each year, compensation costs more THAN the planting budget', a per-year level comparison fixed by the 'than' clause — is the primary parse and is defensible; on it, no trend is asserted and the rationale is right. But 'costs more each year' is idiomatically also read as a trend, and ¶1 surrounds it with trend language ('have been losing ground ever since', 'The flags keep rising'), so a competent student can reach 'rising cost' from the text and will then be told by the rationale that the passage does not say it. The key does not move — A fails as a main-idea option because it is a first-paragraph detail, which is the reason the rationale should have led with — so this is minor, not major. Recommend re-cutting the parenthetical to rest on scope rather than on a contested lexical claim.

findings.claim: The five carried G-STEM majors are real form residues but sit inside the batch16 stance-composition calibration policy, and are weighed here at note severity rather than as an open major.
findings.evidence: BRIEF-ADDENDUM.md, efterhandstillägg 1: "Cross-question stance correlation is REPORTABLE at note severity but does not block, provided (a) the adversarial blind floor is stated explicitly and is no better than 1-in-2, and (b) rule 10 holds. G-STEM should continue to name it; adjudication should not treat it as an open major." Measured floors from verdicts-gstem-r2.jsonl: q1 4→2, q3 4→2, q5 1-in-2 ("C is then the only option covering both halves the stems reveal"), q2 and q4 explicitly recorded as soft leans with "No firm elimination" / "this is narrowing, not answerability". Rule 10 verified independently on the shipped bytes: pick-the-qualified selects the key in 1 of 5 (q4 only); hedged or cautious-sounding options are WRONG on q2 (B 'seems to have', C 'nothing obvious'), q3 (C 'appear to have') and q4 (C 'on the whole, with a few exceptions'), so the inverse heuristic fails too. mech.py re-run confirms M-TELL pass and key strict-longest in 0/5 by the gate's own token metric.
findings.why: No floor in the unit is better than 1-in-2, which is the policy's own boundary, and the residues are of the kind the policy names (a stems sheet that reveals the trial has a five-street group and a twenty-five-street group, with the direction of neither stated after the fleet-repair-2 stem neutralisations). The narrowing is genuine and should stay visible in the record; it is not a kill and, on this brief's severity contract, not a major.

findings.claim: Independent cold solve returns the shipped keys on all five questions with no second defensible answer, but q1 B-vs-C is the thinnest margin in the unit and its defeater is a single hedge word.
findings.evidence: Auditor blind solve, arguing every option: q1 B (A dies on 'believes the remedies mistake where the problem lives' plus the located quote; C dies on 'almost nothing alive'; D unstated). q2 D ('on coarse sand laid nearly twice as deep as the current rule allows'; A dies on 'riding clear over the crates beneath'; B belongs to the separate 'One street failed and taught nobody anything'; C dies on 'The five had one thing in common'). q3 A ('The surveys measure the stones, and only the stones'; B dies on 'four millimetres, the same figure as the year before'; C on ¶5's refusal; D on the knocked-down ¶1 folk theory). q4 B ('On the five streets Fearnbeck’s case is fairly won; on the twenty-five it is not'; A is Askerholt's group's prior view; C inverts 5/25; D dies on the same unattributed verdict). q5 C (B's second half refuted by 'On twenty-five streets the celled flags have stayed within tolerance'). Steelman for q1-C: '…there was almost nothing alive' followed by the flat 'The roots were somewhere else.' reads as a finding that the deep soil held no living root. Defeater: 'almost' explicitly concedes life, and 'The roots were somewhere else' is a locative contrast rather than a census, while the paragraph's conclusion is the key's.
findings.why: Six independent blind solves in the record (G-KEY votes 1 and 2 in the first, r2 and r3 rounds) all returned B and all independently named the same 'almost' defeater, and my own cold read agrees; that is strong evidence against MULTIPLE_DEFENSIBLE. It is still the unit's thinnest margin and G-DISTRACTOR-r2 said so in the same words, so it belongs in the declared residuals rather than nowhere.

findings.claim: The ¶4/¶5 friction the round-3 repair addressed is not fully removed: ¶4 still makes a hedged narrator claim about the bedding under streets nobody has opened, which is exactly the knowledge ¶5 withdraws — and that clause, not the repaired one, is q3-C's real foothold.
findings.evidence: ¶4: "They had been bedded to an older specification, on coarse sand laid nearly twice as deep as the current rule allows, and the roots had evidently found it worth living in; the thin, stiff beds elsewhere were apparently not worth the climb." ¶5: "The surveys measure the stones, and only the stones.… ‘For all we know, the bedding on the good streets is filling with root that has not yet found its strength.’" q3-C: "Their roots appear to have moved down into the loose loam below." Note the hedge match: ¶4's 'apparently' licenses C's 'appear to have'.
findings.why: The friction is legible as designed journalism — ¶4 draws the inference a reader would draw from the surfaces, ¶5 is the corrective that closes the piece and is unambiguously the later and stronger voice. Key A survives cleanly because it is the thing ¶5 states, and C requires an additional unobserved positive claim ('moved down into the loose loam') that no line supports even if the roots are not in the bedding. So this stays a note. But it is a live foothold that survived a repair round advertised as closing it, and G-DISTRACTOR-r3 was right to record it as a residual.

findings.claim: Key A's 'without examining the ground beneath' is looser than the passage strictly licenses, because each of the twenty-five streets has an ordinary side that has been opened.
findings.evidence: ¶4: "On twenty-five streets the celled flags have stayed within tolerance while the ordinary sides opposite have been ground level twice and relaid once." Q3 stem after fleet-repair-2: "What is implied about the twenty-five streets in the trial?" — the referent is the street, which the trial design gives two sides: "Thirty-one streets were rebuilt on cells; the facing pavements, under the same rows of trees, were relaid in the ordinary way." Relaying a pavement necessarily opens the ground beneath it.
findings.why: The key is not endangered: A is scoped to 'The inspectors', who are established in ¶5 as the straightedge-and-wedge-gauge party, and no observation from the ordinary sides is ever reported; the celled sides — the trial's actual subject — were never lifted, which is what ¶5's 'For all we know' presupposes. No other option becomes defensible under the wider reading. Recorded because the fleet-repair-2 stem neutralisation ('the twenty-five streets in the trial') is what widened the referent from the celled pavements to the streets, and the rationale does not address the ordinary sides at all.

findings.claim: All three flagged names re-verify. Every quantitative claim in the originality_note that I could re-run reproduced exactly, including the positive controls, and one rejected-name claim spot-checked clean. No originality claim is refuted.
findings.evidence: en.wikipedia CirrusSearch exact phrase via api.php list=search, run 2026-09-01, ≥1s apart. CONTROL "Pellew" → totalhits 701, top titles ['Edward Pellew, 1st Viscount Exmouth', 'Viscount Exmouth', 'Sir Edward Pellew Group of Islands', 'HMS Pellew (1916)', 'HMS Cavalier'] — reproduces the generator's 701 and its exact title list; control PASSES. "Askerholt" → 0. "Bronwen Askerholt" → 0. "Fearnbeck" → 0. "Osmund Fearnbeck" → 0. "Welbrace" → 0. "Sidonie Welbrace" → 0. Given-name sanity: "Bronwen" → 1454, "Osmund" → 955, "Sidonie" → 887 (real given names, as the log implies). Nominatim: CONTROL q=Flarken&countrycodes=se → 10 places (Luleå, Härjedalen, Boden, Kalix, Vindeln) — PASSES; q=Askerholt → 0, q=Fearnbeck → 0, q=Welbrace → 0. Quoted WebSearch: "Askerholt" → no exact-string bearer, neighbours are Asker (Norway), Asker station, Asker SK, Asker Fotball — matching the log's disclosure verbatim; "Fearnbeck" → no bearer, neighbours Fearn, Easter Fearn, Fearne, Routenbeck, Fulbeck and the FreenBeck fandom tag — matching the log including the fandom disclosure; "Welbrace" → no person/place/publication bearer, and the two disclosed items both surface (welbrace.com parked domain registered 2020 with ~5,032,444 world rank, and Wembrace Biopharma Pvt Ltd, India); combined "Bronwen Askerholt" OR "Osmund Fearnbeck" OR "Sidonie Welbrace" → no full-name bearer, only given-name neighbours including Bronwen Astor, exactly as logged. Rejected-name spot check: "Rakeworth" → dungeoneer.com generated village/coastal-town name lists plus a neighborwho.com Henrico VA property-records page, corroborating both halves of the stated rejection ground.
findings.why: The generator explicitly refused to certify these names ('NOTHING here is a certificate: every kept name is FLAGGED FOR V-FINAL RE-VERIFICATION'). The re-run confirms rather than refutes: same endpoints, same session discipline, controls first, and the disclosed near-misses (Asker, FreenBeck, welbrace.com, Wembrace) all reproduce, which is itself evidence that the log was written from real results rather than assumed. Law 16 is satisfied for Bronwen Askerholt, Osmund Fearnbeck and Sidonie Welbrace.

findings.claim: Every repair_log ticket verifies byte-exactly against the round-0 generator file, no unclaimed edit exists anywhere in the unit, and the keys are unchanged across all three rounds.
findings.evidence: Diff of gen-elf-long.json (round 0, candidate_id 'PLACEHOLDER') against candidates/elf-b18-001.json. PASSAGE: exactly two sentence-level changes — "The five streets are his, fairly won; the twenty-five are not." → "On the five streets Fearnbeck’s case is fairly won; on the twenty-five it is not." (r1 retirement, amended by r3's naming) and "And on five, the survey found exactly what Fearnbeck had said it would find – …" → "And on five, when the flags were lifted, the crews found exactly what Fearnbeck had said they would find – …" (r3 reattribution, with 'and relaid' correctly omitted so 'Those five have since been relaid…' still carries the relaying once). This also corroborates r2's 'Passage untouched'. QUESTIONS: exactly the nine claimed r2 edits and nothing else — q1-C ('entirely without roots' → 'bare of living root'), q2 stem ('where the treatment failed' → 'in the trial'), q2-B (hedged actor swap), q3 stem ('where the treatment has worked' → 'the twenty-five streets in the trial'), q3-A/B/C rebuilt, q4-C ('bore it out in full' → 'bore him out on the whole, with a few exceptions'), q5-B ('finally beat the tree roots' → 'why the remedies keep failing'). KEYS: B, D, A, B, C at round 0 and at ship. 'are his' occurs twice in the file, both inside repair_log provenance strings, and nowhere in the passage or questions — the G-REGISTER retirement holds. Absolutizer sweep over all twenty options: 'entirely', 'at all', 'never' all absent; only q2-C's 'nothing', distractor-side. mech.py re-run on the shipped file: M-SCHEMA / M-BANDS / M-TELL / M-FORM / M-ECHO / M-PLAGIARISM all pass, zero findings, M-ECHO indexed 114 shipped units. Band numbers reproduce under mech's own tokenizer: 795 words, 36 sentences, mean 22.1, 5 paragraphs; token ratios 1.08 / 1.44 / 1.09 / 1.56 / 1.40 and key strict-longest 0/5 all confirmed. Max shared n-gram between any option and the passage: 0 at n≥4. blind/, stems/ and distractor/ sheets machine-verified in sync with the shipped candidate, with no key, rationale, generator_meta or family leakage into blind/ or stems/.
findings.why: The repair rounds are where drift enters, and this is the check the brief asked for. Three rounds of surgery on a live unit produced no orphan edit, no key movement, no reintroduction of the retired construction, and no sheet desync. The one residue the byte check does surface — a rationale quote that never matched — is charged separately above.

findings.claim: generator_meta.hedge_balance appeals to a 'completed absolutizer family adopted after batch17' that the shipped mech.py does not implement; the conclusion drawn from it is nevertheless correct.
findings.evidence: BRIEF-ADDENDUM.md efterhandstïllägg 2 records the family as completed with 'nothing', 'nobody', 'no one', 'ingenting', 'ingenstans', 'uteslutande' added and states 'semantik dokumenterad i mech.py'. gates/scripts/mech.py _ABSOLUTIZERS contains none of those six tokens; all six copies of mech.py on this machine (main checkout plus five worktrees) are byte-identical at 25116 bytes and none carries them. hedge_balance: "q2-C still carries ‘nothing’ from the completed absolutizer family adopted after batch17, on the DISTRACTOR side only, so M-FORM cannot fire."
findings.why: No effect on this unit in either direction: M-FORM fires only when EVERY distractor carries an absolutizer and the key carries none, and q2-A and q2-B carry none under either version of the list, so M-FORM passes with or without the addendum tokens — as the re-run confirms. Recorded because the unit's declared form safety cites a policy the gate code does not enforce, which is a pipeline-level gap a future unit could actually trip over.
